chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: A successful jam night at the House That Jazz Built
summary: On 25 July they held a packed event, with local musicians, and elected Amos president of the musicians' group.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: We're back at the House That Jazz Built in South Bronx, and it's Friday, July the 25th and Maxine was just telling me about the great success of the benefit for the House That Jazz Built at Gulliver's in West Patterson, New Jersey, two nights ago.

Well, we had a ball. I got out there about 8:30 and I was surprised to see that there were quite a few cars in the parking lot at the time and a party that ended just before we did -- the party that was arriving just as we were in town and they had been down in The Bahamas and they said that they had heard the show that I had done previously and I guess they saw an ad in the paper so they showed up.
Well, it was in the New York Times last Sunday.
Well, see, I didn't know that. It was great. But it was a ball, the place was

jam-packed and Amos got the bass player, Lou Morrow, who lives out that way and Rudy Walker, a drummer who lives out that way and we brought Stash O'Loughlin, a piano player, Alan Hanlon on guitar. Alan and Flo Hanlon are members of the House that Jazz Built. Flo sings, and so we had quite a show.
Florence sang, the bass players wife, Lynn Morrow, she sang, Estella Williams, one of our members, sang and we had Carmen Leggio -- Wilma De Ric our secretary brought Carmen Leggio and his wife.

He plays tenor and she plays flute. They played. I, of course, sang and we have a young man, blues singer, Claudio Maxwell who sang -- he's a blues singer, he sang. And after he got through he practically took over and acted as the M.C.

And we transacted a little business. We elected Amos the President of the House that Jazz Built, which he accepted and it was a real ball and at the end of the evening Amos turned over a check for $1,031 to the House that Jazz Built.
